protein_interactions_documented.relationship: NF1 protein functions as RAS-GAP, directly regulating RAS GTPase activity. Loss of NF1 leads to constitutive RAS/MAPK activation.
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: Primary disease mechanism in NF1 - constitutive pathway activation drives tumor formation

protein_interactions_documented.relationship: TOP2A-induced DNA damage activates TP53-mediated apoptotic pathways in cancer cells
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: Critical for doxorubicin anti-tumor efficacy through DNA damage → p53 → apoptosis axis

protein_interactions_documented.relationship: ATM senses TOP2A-induced DNA double-strand breaks and activates checkpoint signaling
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: ATM status affects tumor sensitivity to doxorubicin; enhances efficacy through checkpoint activation

protein_interactions_documented.relationship: TOP2B inhibition in cardiomyocytes leads to mitochondrial dysfunction and ROS generation
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: Primary driver of doxorubicin cardiotoxicity; selective TOP2B inhibition could reduce toxicity

protein_interactions_documented.relationship: SOD2 converts superoxide to H2O2; CAT subsequently degrades H2O2 to water and oxygen
protein_interactions_documented.evidence: oxidative stress response pathway - sequential enzymatic cascade
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: Coordinated antioxidant defense - both required for complete ROS detoxification in cardiomyocytes

protein_interactions_documented.relationship: SOD2 and GPX1 work in parallel antioxidant pathways - SOD2 in mitochondria, GPX1 neutralizes H2O2 and lipid peroxides
protein_interactions_documented.evidence: oxidative stress response - complementary ROS defense systems
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: Dual cardioprotective mechanism - enhancing either could reduce doxorubicin cardiac injury

protein_interactions_documented.relationship: Both ABC transporters export doxorubicin from cells via different mechanisms - direct efflux (ABCB1) vs glutathione conjugate export (ABCC1)
protein_interactions_documented.evidence: ABC transporter pathway, multidrug resistance mechanisms
protein_interactions_documented.relevance: Redundant resistance mechanisms - inhibiting one may not overcome resistance if other is active

pathways.name: RAS/MAPK signaling pathway
pathways.description: NF1 negatively regulates RAS by stimulating GTPase activity. Loss of NF1 causes constitutive RAS/MAPK activation, driving cell proliferation and tumor formation in NF1 disease.
pathways.therapeutic_implication: Hyperactive RAS/MAPK signaling in NF1-deficient tumors may alter response to DNA-damaging agents like doxorubicin

pathways.name: DNA damage response pathway
pathways.description: ATM senses DNA double-strand breaks induced by TOP2A inhibition, phosphorylates TP53, leading to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in cancer cells
pathways.therapeutic_implication: Intact DNA damage response pathway is critical for doxorubicin efficacy. TP53 mutations or ATM deficiency may confer resistance.

pathways.name: Oxidative stress response and ROS detoxification
pathways.description: Coordinated antioxidant enzyme system. SOD2 converts mitochondrial superoxide to H2O2. GPX1 reduces H2O2 and lipid peroxides using glutathione. CAT degrades H2O2 to water and oxygen.
pathways.therapeutic_implication: Upregulation of these cardioprotective genes could reduce doxorubicin-induced oxidative cardiac injury without affecting anti-tumor efficacy (tumor selectivity)

pathways.name: ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux
pathways.description: ATP-dependent efflux pumps export doxorubicin from cells. ABCB1 directly transports drug. ABCC1 exports glutathione conjugates and drug metabolites.
pathways.therapeutic_implication: ABC transporter inhibition could overcome resistance but may increase systemic toxicity. Tumor-selective inhibition strategies needed.
pathways.evidence: ensembl annotations, literature on multidrug resistance

pathways.name: Topoisomerase II-mediated DNA damage
pathways.description: Doxorubicin inhibits both TOP2A (in proliferating cancer cells) and TOP2B (in cardiomyocytes), stabilizing DNA-topoisomerase cleavage complexes and causing DNA strand breaks
pathways.therapeutic_implication: Critical pathway bifurcation: TOP2A inhibition = efficacy (tumor DNA damage), TOP2B inhibition = toxicity (cardiac DNA damage and mitochondrial dysfunction). Isoform-selective TOP2A inhibitors could preserve efficacy while reducing cardiotoxicity.

pathways.name: mTOR signaling pathway
pathways.description: NF1 loss leads to dysregulated mTOR signaling downstream of RAS activation, contributing to increased cell growth and metabolism in NF1 tumors
pathways.therapeutic_implication: mTOR pathway alterations in NF1 disease may affect cellular stress responses and drug sensitivity
pathways.evidence: NF1 disease literature, relevant_pathways in phase2

interactions.relevance: NF1-deficient tumors with TP53 mutations may be resistant to doxorubicin due to impaired apoptotic response

interactions.relevance: TP53 status predicts doxorubicin efficacy; wild-type TP53 enhances response

interactions.relevance: ATM→TP53 axis critical for doxorubicin-induced cell death; defects in either confer resistance

interactions.relevance: Dual ABC transporter expression provides robust resistance mechanism

candidate_targets.rationale: TOP2B is the primary driver of doxorubicin cardiotoxicity but not required for anti-tumor efficacy (which depends on TOP2A). Selective TOP2B inhibition or cardioprotective strategies targeting TOP2B-mediated mitochondrial dysfunction could reduce toxicity while preserving efficacy.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: Develop TOP2A-selective inhibitors, or cardioprotective agents that block TOP2B-mediated mitochondrial damage

candidate_targets.rationale: Mitochondrial superoxide dismutase provides cardioprotection against doxorubicin-induced oxidative stress. Upregulation in cardiomyocytes (but not tumor cells) could reduce toxicity. SOD2 interacts with CAT and GPX1 in coordinated ROS detoxification network.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: Gene therapy, small molecule activators, or exercise/dietary interventions to upregulate cardiac SOD2 expression before chemotherapy
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich SOD2 annotation, oxidative stress pathway

candidate_targets.rationale: Works downstream of SOD2 to degrade H2O2. Appears in oxidative stress pathway with SOD2 and GPX1. Cardiac-specific catalase upregulation could provide additive cardioprotection.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: Catalase mimetics, antioxidant supplementation, or cardiac-targeted gene therapy
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich CAT annotation, sequential ROS detoxification with SOD2

candidate_targets.rationale: Glutathione peroxidase neutralizes H2O2 and lipid peroxides. Parallel pathway to CAT. Lower GPX1 activity correlates with increased cardiac damage from doxorubicin.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: Selenium supplementation (GPX1 cofactor), glutathione precursors (N-acetylcysteine), or GPX1 gene therapy
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich GPX1 annotation, oxidative stress pathway
candidate_targets.note: STRING ID not resolved due to search failure; may use alternative identifier

candidate_targets.rationale: Central mediator of doxorubicin efficacy through DNA damage→apoptosis pathway. Interacts with both ATM (upstream activator) and TOP2A (DNA damage inducer). TP53 status predicts treatment response.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: TP53 status should be evaluated as predictive biomarker for doxorubicin response in NF1-associated tumors. Wild-type TP53 predicts better efficacy. TP53-mutant tumors may require alternative strategies.
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich TP53 annotation, DNA damage response pathway

candidate_targets.rationale: DNA damage sensor that activates TP53-mediated apoptosis. ATM status affects tumor sensitivity to anthracyclines. Appears in DNA damage response pathway with TP53 and TOP2A.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: ATM status evaluation as predictive biomarker. ATM-deficient tumors may be resistant to doxorubicin but potentially sensitive to PARP inhibitors (synthetic lethality).
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich ATM annotation, DNA damage response pathway

candidate_targets.rationale: Major doxorubicin resistance mechanism. Direct drug efflux pump. Overexpression in tumors reduces intracellular drug accumulation. Works redundantly with ABCC1.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: ABC transporter inhibitors (e.g., verapamil, cyclosporine) or tumor-selective delivery systems to bypass efflux. Monitor expression as resistance biomarker.
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich ABCB1 annotation, ABC transporter pathway

candidate_targets.rationale: Exports doxorubicin-glutathione conjugates. Complementary resistance mechanism to ABCB1. Dual transporter expression provides robust resistance.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: Combination ABC transporter inhibition or alternative drug delivery approaches. Expression profiling for treatment stratification.
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich ABCC1 annotation, ABC transporter pathway

candidate_targets.rationale: Primary disease gene. Loss causes constitutive RAS/MAPK activation. RAS pathway status may alter cellular stress responses and drug sensitivity. NF1-deficient tumors show altered metabolic and proliferative signatures.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: RAS/MAPK pathway hyperactivation in NF1 tumors may affect doxorubicin response. Potential combination strategies: MEK inhibitors + doxorubicin to target both RAS pathway and DNA damage. Evaluate if RAS pathway status predicts anthracycline sensitivity in NF1 disease.
candidate_targets.evidence: phase2_enrich NF1 annotation, RAS/MAPK pathway, disease pathophysiology

candidate_targets.rationale: Peroxiredoxins appear in oxidative stress pathway alongside SOD2, GPX1, CAT. PRDX3 is mitochondrial (like SOD2) and could provide additional cardioprotection against doxorubicin-induced ROS.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: Explore as additional cardioprotective targets if primary antioxidant strategies (SOD2/CAT/GPX1) prove insufficient
candidate_targets.evidence: pathway knowledge - oxidative stress response network

candidate_targets.rationale: DNA repair genes in the same pathway as ATM and TP53. BRCA-deficient tumors show altered sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents. May interact with TOP2A-induced damage response.
candidate_targets.therapeutic_strategy: BRCA status evaluation in NF1-associated tumors may predict anthracycline response. BRCA-deficient tumors may show altered doxorubicin sensitivity.

key_relationships: Activated by ATM in response to TOP2A-induced DNA damage
genes_in_multiple_contexts.clinical_implication: TP53 wild-type status should be prioritized biomarker for NF1 patients receiving doxorubicin

key_relationships: Causes mitochondrial DNA damage in cardiomyocytes
genes_in_multiple_contexts.clinical_implication: TOP2B-selective inhibition or cardioprotection is highest-priority strategy for improving therapeutic index

key_relationships: Works with CAT and GPX1 in coordinated ROS defense
Mitochondrial localization matches site of doxorubicin ROS generation
Does NOT interfere with tumor cell killing
genes_in_multiple_contexts.clinical_implication: Cardiac-specific SOD2 upregulation could reduce toxicity without compromising efficacy

crosstalk_genes: potential: TP53 (can be regulated by MAPK)
pathway_crosstalk.implication: Constitutive RAS/MAPK activation in NF1 disease may alter cellular stress responses and affect doxorubicin efficacy. Combination MEK inhibitor + doxorubicin may be synergistic.
Glutathione metabolism links antioxidant defense and drug resistance. Strategies to enhance cardiac antioxidants must consider potential impact on tumor drug resistance.
This is the core efficacy pathway: TOP2A inhibition → DNA damage → ATM activation → TP53 → apoptosis. Any disruption reduces efficacy.

selective_toxicity_opportunities.rationale: TOP2A (proliferating cells/tumors) vs TOP2B (cardiomyocytes). Selective TOP2A inhibitors preserve efficacy, reduce toxicity.
Enhance SOD2/CAT/GPX1 only in cardiomyocytes, not in tumor cells. Protects heart without reducing tumor oxidative stress.
selective_toxicity_opportunities.feasibility: medium - requires tissue-targeted delivery or cardiac-specific promoters

selective_toxicity_opportunities.rationale: Inhibit ABCB1/ABCC1 to enhance tumor drug accumulation without increasing cardiac exposure
selective_toxicity_opportunities.feasibility: low - achieving tumor selectivity challenging; systemic inhibition increases toxicity
